newsitem.title: FRANCE: Generale des Eaux to restructure SGE.
newsitem.headline: Generale des Eaux to restructure SGE.

text.p: The chairman of French utilities company Cie Generale des Eaux (CGE) unveiled on Monday plans to restructure its loss-making Societe Generale d'Entreprises (SGE) construction subsidiary.
Jean-Marie Messier told reporters that CGE would transfer its GTIE and Santerne electrical installations units to SGE, to create with SGE's SDEL a group with 11 billion francs of annual sales.
The deal values GTIE and Santerne at 11 times net profit and sets a net asset value for SGE of 160 francs per share.
SGE will issue 10 million new shares in the deal, which will be earnings positive and will boost SGE's 1997 EPS by six francs per share, Messier said.

Along with other restructuring measures in roadbuilding and construction, Messier plans for SGE to return to a "significant level" of profit in 1997 and to make it "radically different and attractive."
Roadbuilding firms Cochery, Viafrance and SGE-VBU will be brought into SGE to create a group with annual sales of 11 billion francs.
The concentration follows difficult conditions, with the market falling 3.5 percent in 1995 and 10 percent by June 1996, which have hit volume and margins, he said.
The construction arm will be reorganized with SGE buying 40 percent of the capital of Compagnie Generale de Batiment et de Construction (CBC), which is currently 100 percent owned by CGE.

Difficulties in the French building and public works sector made it hard to run three separate construction companies -- Sogea and Campenon Bernard at SGE and CBC at Generale des Eaux -- which was why it was necessary to consolidate, Messier said.
Further reorganizing steps will be decided by the end of 1996. The new SGE is expected to have annual sales of 52 billion francs in 1997 and have greater synergies and risk control.

The group has signed an agreement for a pool of German banks to buy three troubled Berlin properties being built by SGE for around one billion marks, which will mean SGE making provisions of 400 million francs.
